problem: A shared import function must be simplified, but several callers depend on undocumented edge-case behavior.
goal: Reduce implementation complexity without changing accepted inputs, outputs, or failure atomicity.
ifr: The import function becomes simpler using existing tests and adapters while all observed caller contracts and data-safety invariants remain unchanged.
invariants: No partial write is committed after a failed import
Existing supported input formats remain accepted

claims.statement: Three production callers invoke the shared import function.
claims.source: rg call-site inventory at frozen commit

claims.statement: Caller-specific adapters can preserve edge-case behavior.

solutions.mechanism: Move caller-specific normalization into explicit adapters and keep one narrow transaction core.
risks: An undocumented behavior may be omitted from an adapter

solutions.mechanism: Run the old and new implementations against a frozen corpus and switch only after output equivalence is established.
risks: The frozen corpus may not cover rare production inputs

verification: Compare old and new outputs on representative and adversarial inputs
recommended_next_step: Build a read-only caller and behavior inventory before changing the shared function.
open_questions: Which observed behaviors are contractual rather than accidental?
